title: Hack Wave
subtitle: This week in Bitcoin & Nostr news

topics.title: Live Dashboard & Market
topics.description: A red Uptober, a Fed hold with two hawks, an election-night dip, and Strategy back to buying

slides.heading: Live Dashboard
slides.body: Where Bitcoin sits right now. The full dashboards:

slides.heading: Market: Red Uptober, Blue Congress
slides.body: October closed down about 7%, a second red October. Election night dipped under $76K; this afternoon it was back over $80K.
bullets: Fed held at 3.75–4%, 10–2. Both dissents, Cook and Hammack, wanted a hike
ETFs: October -$516M. Nov 2 -$399M (IBIT -$405M), Nov 3 -$116M
Strategy +811 BTC, now 849,327. Another $208M STRC buyback. STRC pays daily since Nov 1. CFO Kang out Nov 5
Tether's Ardoino: "give or take 150,000 bitcoin." The Q3 attestation shows ~100,000
Next Technology may sell all 5,833 BTC, citing Binance and quantum. Coinbase bought its 18,000th coin on the whitepaper's 18th birthday

topics.title: Hack Wave: Binance and the Copycats
topics.description: The biggest crypto hack ever, Binance's own post-mortem, what could and couldn't be frozen, and two copycat hits the same week

slides.heading: Hack Wave: Binance, $6.4B, Week Two
slides.body: Oct 29, 4:20 PM Eastern: the hot wallet started emptying. 18,270 BTC plus XRP, SOL and OP. The largest crypto theft ever.
bullets: Elliptic: $2.85B frozen, 44%. Stablecoins were 54% of the loot. $3.21B still sits in attacker addresses, mostly ETH and BTC
Elliptic: "ETH and BTC cannot be frozen, so there is no rush"
FBI: North Korea's TraderTraitor. Kim Yo Jong: "absurd rhetoric"
Binance covered it from SAFU and company funds. 98% replenished by Oct 31. Withdrawals back
Question: freezable stablecoins limited the damage. Feature, or warning?

links.label: Korea Times: FBI names North Korea

slides.heading: The Post-Mortem Is a Job Interview
slides.body: Binance's initial findings, Nov 3. A months-long campaign, not one phish. Every step was an ordinary developer habit.
bullets: June: a DevOps engineer installs a tampered Homebrew build of "a popular AI coding tool" from a search result
September: a fake recruiter and "CEO" video interview. The take-home repo, run on a work laptop, swaps out pyenv
Oct 20: an internal AI tool reaches two more engineers and turns up a container deployment token
Oct 29: a malicious container hits the signing service. EIP-7702 delegations drain until 00:10 UTC Oct 30
MPC meant no single key could revoke fast. Question: what would multisig with humans in the loop have changed?

slides.heading: Copycats, Regulators, and Where You Keep It
slides.body: Three exchange-scale hacks and a BTCPay sweep in one week.
bullets: Mercado Bitcoin, Nov 2: ~US$38M involved, US$11M frozen with Tether, Circle, Paxos, Chainalysis. Customers covered
ZachXBT: a separate $106M+ theft from an EU firm, swapped to ETH and partly XMR. French-speaking, not Lazarus
South Korea's FSC called exchanges in: raise the cold-wallet share, monitor around the clock, add reserves
calle (Cashu): nothing on exchanges, only small amounts on Lightning nodes, BTCPay or mints
Question for the room: where does your stack live tonight?

topics.title: Security Desk: Patch Week
topics.description: Core's first public advisories under its new policy, a 9.8 kernel bug that hits every Linux node, Lightning patches, and BTCPay servers drained

slides.heading: Security Desk: Core's First Three Advisories
slides.body: Last week: the new disclosure policy. Oct 28: the first advisories under it. Fixes in 32.1, 31.2, 30.4 and 29.5.
bullets: TCP urgent data, CVE-2026-117350, Medium: any peer can run a Windows, macOS or BSD node out of memory. Linux unaffected
Paused pre-BIP31 peers, CVE-2026-117349, Medium: send queue grows without limit, 2 MB/h per inbound peer
Undo-file overflow, Low: a miner could force a shutdown on a later reorg. Impractical on 64-bit
Found by an LLM scan: Elias Rohrer's Project Loupe at Spiral, validated by Gregory Sanders. Oct 23 found, Oct 27 shipped
Hamilton: some findings sat in the Red Team before the blast radius was clear. Question: is "scan-found" the same as "easily discoverable"?

slides.heading: A 9.8 in the Kernel
slides.body: CVE-2026-98432: a use-after-free in Linux TCP, remote code execution, CVSS 9.8. The demo exploit rides MPTCP, on by default in Go programs like LND.
bullets: Any Linux node or relay with open ports. Fix the kernel, LND 0.21.6 / 0.20.7, or `sysctl net.mptcp.enabled=0` for now
umbrelOS 2.0.1 and StartOS 0.4.1 shipped it. Raspberry Pi gets a firewall block until a fixed Pi kernel exists
Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04: fixed kernels only in -proposed. Ubuntu: disabling MPTCP is not a fix
Eclair 0.14.6: "can be exploited by malicious nodes." Splices no longer spend unconfirmed inputs
LND 0.21.5 final. Zeus 13.2.4 thanks Bitcoin Red Team and Anthropic for scans. CLN 26.04.1 fixes a crash loop

slides.heading: BTCPay Servers Drained
slides.body: Nov 1, 8:46 AM Eastern: the first hot wallet drained. Servers on 2.4.1 or older, hit through a new route to the bug fixed in 2.4.2 in August.
bullets: The advisory: upgrading alone isn't enough. New seed, sweep, fresh VM, old box offline with its logs, rotate every credential
Keys on a hardware wallet or off the server: safe. 2.4.2 and later: no impact seen
The attacker address: 20.36 BTC in 837 outputs by this afternoon. BTCPay: not a confirmed loss total
BTCPay: "the rise in automated attacks using AI" means patch as they ship. 2.4.7 alone closed 85 findings from Anthropic's scanner
The study: 71% of LND nodes exposed at the August disclosure still ran an affected release two months later

topics.title: Wallet Watch: Fee Bumps and Implants
topics.description: A rogue Electrum server steals on fee-bump, exploited in the wild; Cake has the same bug; and the CryptoBilis implant story reaches Trezor

slides.heading: Wallet Watch: The Fee Bump That Pays the Attacker
slides.body: Electrum 4.8.3, CVE-2026-117601, High. A rogue server swallows your payment, shows a look-alike zero-fee transaction, and waits for you to bump the fee.
bullets: The fake address matches the real one's last four characters. Light clients don't check its signatures. Exploited in the wild, one loss
Not affected: anyone on their own or a trusted server
Cake Wallet: same bug class, disclosed Oct 19. 6.5.2 doesn't mention a fix. Super: "Any node a user is connected to can perform this theft"
Sparrow 2.5.6 and Nunchuk 2.9.3 ported Electrum's check
Trezor, Oct 30: a credible implant in a Safe 5 from CryptoBilis. Bought a Trezor there since March? New seed, now

topics.title: Policy Corner: The Midterms Reset the Clock
topics.description: Democrats take both chambers and TD Cowen sees no CLARITY Act for two years; Bhutan's new city central bank may hold crypto; Moscow lists spot bitcoin

slides.heading: Policy Corner: CLARITY Gets the Lame Duck or Nothing
slides.body: Democrats won the House and the Senate last night. TD Cowen's Jaret Seiberg, before the votes: "we do not expect the Clarity Act to pass over the next two years."
bullets: CLARITY passed the House 294–134 in July 2025, failed Senate cloture 49–50 on Sept 15. Dies Jan 3 unless the lame duck moves it
Warren expected at Senate Banking, Waters at House Financial Services. Crypto groups spent over $200M this cycle
Florida: Governor-elect Donalds backs a state bitcoin reserve. The 2026 bills died. He takes office in January
Bhutan, Nov 2: Gelephu's regulator becomes a central bank that may hold digital assets. Already a top sovereign holder
Moscow Exchange: spot BTC, ETH, USDT from Dec 1. Custodial, retail capped at 300,000 rubles a year
slides.linkLabel: Bitcoin Magazine: TD Cowen on CLARITY

topics.title: Lightning Corner: Liquid Is 1:1 Again
topics.description: Liquid's reserves fully restored, LN Markets takes BOLT12, Cashu's mint ships a security release, and a Japanese company raises equity in bitcoin for routing liquidity

slides.heading: Lightning Corner: Liquid Closes the Book
slides.body: Four second-layer updates, one of them the end of a story we've followed since September.
bullets: Liquid, Nov 2: every L-BTC backed 1:1 again. A 300 BTC top-up confirmed that afternoon. Check the Proof of Reserves with your own node
LN Markets, Nov 3: BOLT12 offers for deposits and withdrawals. One reusable code instead of a fresh invoice
Cashu nutshell 0.22.0: security fixes, BIP-39 mint seeds, caching without Redis. Back up before the DB migration
Japan Bitcoin Industry raised ¥800M paid entirely in bitcoin. ANAP: 65.85 BTC for 19.96%, and the coins become routing liquidity
NutNovember: Cashu's month-long hackathon started Nov 1, over 1M sats in prizes

topics.title: Nostr This Week: Private by Default
topics.description: Damus makes private DMs the default, Amethyst turns notes into apps, Amber goes desktop, a relay-on-your-phone CVE, and five open NIP proposals

slides.heading: Nostr This Week: Damus 1.18, Amethyst 1.21, Amber on Desktop
slides.body: The two biggest clients and the most-used signer all shipped.
bullets: Damus 1.18 (Oct 27): new DMs use NIP-17, so relays can't see who talks to whom. NIP-04 off by default. Advanced search, storage cap
Amethyst 1.21.0 (Nov 1): napplets run inside notes, webxdc apps, game cartridges (Quake III), PressStr ebooks
Amber 7.0.0-pre2: first desktop signer, Linux/macOS/Windows. Local relay at 127.0.0.1:7777 so same-machine apps skip public relays
Jumble v26.11.1 lands on Android, DMs off by default
Citrine CVE-2026-107045: any Android app can read your on-phone relay's event store. Metadata and ciphertext. No fix noted yet

slides.heading: Five NIPs on the Table
slides.body: All open pull requests. Nothing here is merged or in a client yet.
bullets: NIP-05 over DNS (#2527): a TXT record at _nip05.<domain> points to another provider. Clients try DNS only after a 404
NIP-D9 (#2531): a signed no_delete marker so a shared key can't delete what others still need
Zapstore spec (#2526): fiatjaf's draft for the app store
Zaps over BIP-321 (#2521), from the Bark team: pay a zap over Ark, Lightning or on-chain, wallet picks the rail
Batten's NYT-ad crowdfund: more came via Nostr than X. Question: which of these will a client actually build?

topics.title: AI Corner: Agents That Pay in Sats
topics.description: New section. Agents paying over Lightning and Ark, a node OS that talks MCP, and AI on both sides of this week's exploits

slides.heading: AI Corner: Agents With Wallets
slides.body: A new standing section, because AI keeps showing up in the Bitcoin news. First: tools that let an agent pay in sats, no custodial API key.
bullets: barkget (Second): "curl for L402 and Ark 402." Pays paywalls from a self-custodial Bark wallet, shares a ledger with bark-mcp
StartOS 0.4.1: an MCP server at /mcp with named, revocable bearer tokens. Your node box, driven by an agent, on your terms
OpenAgents: Pylon nodes sell compute and agent labor for bitcoin, coordinated over a Nostr relay. Apache-2.0
Sats for Bots lists the agent-payment MCP servers side by side: Alby, bark-mcp, Spark, 402-mcp
Counterpoint from Spiral's payments report: stablecoins are winning agent payments too. Can sats catch up?

slides.heading: Both Sides of the Exploit
slides.body: Count this week's patch notes: AI found most of the bugs, and the Binance attackers used it to get in.
bullets: Found by scans: Core's two Medium bugs (Project Loupe), BTCPay's 85 findings, the kernel 9.8, Zeus's hardening
Used by attackers: a tampered AI coding tool got the first Binance foothold; an internal AI tool found the next two engineers
Rob Hamilton, Freedom Tech DC: Bitcoin Red Team moved to open-weight models. One found the Coldcard exploit for about $1 once it was public
Maple AI: "Local is the goal. But most people can't run DeepSeek or Kimi at home yet." Open models in verifiable enclaves until then
Question: when bugs get found by the thousand, what does a home node runner do?

links.label: Maple AI on local vs enclaves

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Cashu Card
topics.description: Offline tap-to-pay bitcoin ecash on an off-the-shelf smart card. Open source, experimental, and you can build one this week

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Cashu Card
slides.body: Ecash you can tap. An applet on a blank NXP J3R180 smart card; your wallet loads ecash onto it. A merchant's phone takes the tap offline and settles with the mint later.
bullets: A tap: the phone names the pieces it wants, the card signs once and burns them, the phone checks the mint's signatures offline
128 slots per card. The key is born on the chip and never leaves. MIT, draft spec NUT-CCP
Try it: blank J3R180 cards from Amazon or CardLogix, flash the applet with the Provisioner app (iOS/Android beta)
Limits: lose the card, lose the balance. Three wrong PINs lock it. Merchant carries double-spend risk until settlement
Few phones, one card model, no independent review yet. A demo, not a savings account. Super's "bearer instruments ftw" in hardware

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Binance's $6.4B hack started with two everyday dev habits: a take-home interview repo and a tool installed from a search result. Here's the reflex

slides.heading: Quick Tip: The Homework Is the Hack
slides.body: Two ordinary habits opened Binance: an AI coding tool installed from a search result, and a recruiter's "assignment" repo run on a work laptop.
bullets: Take-home code, "test this repo," "run our SDK": a throwaway VM. Never a machine with wallets, SSH keys or API tokens
Install tools by typing the official URL or from your package manager. Never from a search ad
A recruiter who wants you to run something before the offer is the attack
Ubuntu node? Run `uname -r` and compare with the fixed kernels. On 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04 they're only in -proposed
Self-hosted BTCPay ever on 2.4.1 or older? Rebuild on a new seed tonight. Upgrading doesn't evict a guest
